root_idea.summary: The root centers on occupying or preoccupying, in contrast to emptiness or leisure.
root_idea.development: The basic idea of occupying another or being occupied extends to diversion of attention, business and preoccupation, states of engagement, resource-use, and specialized senses involving substances taking effect.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Form I perfect citation form شَغَلَ rather than the Quranic feminine singular token شَغَلَتْ.
Displayed as the Quran-attested noun شُغُلٌ.

senses.definition: To busy, occupy, or engage someone, diverting them from something.
senses.usage_conditions: A transitive Form I verb; the diversion-from nuance is especially expressed with عَنْ. The Quranic occurrence is an active form referring to being kept busy.

senses.definition: An engrossing preoccupation or circumstance that absorbs and distracts a person’s attention.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic expression شُغُلٍ فَاكِهُونَ, it denotes an engrossing state or occupation; the sense may involve being made forgetful or unmindful of other matters.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Business, occupation, or employment; the opposite of leisure.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The related vowel forms شُغُلٌ and شَغَلٌ are also recorded. The preoccupying or distracting extension overlaps the Quranic nominal sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To occupy a place, resource, or supply so that it is kept from another; hence, to have enough for oneself.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested in expressions concerning pasture or water being occupied and thereby unavailable to another.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Busy, occupied, or employed; engaged with something so as to be diverted from another matter.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Related forms include مَشْغُولٌ, مُشْتَغِلٌ, and مُشْتَغَلٌ. شَغَّالٌ expresses intensive or habitual busyness, أَشْغَلُ is comparative or superlative, and مَا أَشْغَلَهُ is an anomalous exclamative meaning how greatly someone is busied.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To busy oneself with something, or to occupy one another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: May be construed with عَنْ for turning oneself away from or keeping oneself occupied away from someone or something.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To spread through or pervade, of poison; to enter and take effect, of medicine.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized construction describing a substance penetrating or producing its effect in a person or thing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One or something that busies, occupies, or diverts another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a person or to an affair; its plural may refer to busifying or distracting affairs.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Reaped grain or wheat collected together at the place where it is threshed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized agricultural noun, also associated with بَيْدَرٌ and كُدْسٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A thing with which one is busied or occupied.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An أُفْعُولَةٌ formation from the occupation sense; it can also function as a synonym of شُغْلٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A thing that causes someone to be busied or occupied.
Occupied, engaged, or in use in specialized applications.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A person may be occupied with an unprofitable pursuit; a young woman may be married; property may be devoted to commerce; and a house may be inhabited.
